5	**Version-support registry** (`lib/cyrus/versions/registry.{ts,json}`, R0 day 1). One row per Minecraft version: family, `javaRelease` (21 for 1.21.x, 25 for 26.x), `status` (supported / preview / legacy / blocked), `buildable` (true only for what the build service compiles today: 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11), exact `paperCoordinate` (null for 26.x until a stable build is pinned), resource/data pack formats (null = unverified, consumers fail closed) and capability flags (`itemModelDefinitions` 1.21.4+, `dialogApi` 1.21.7+, `adventure5`). `resourcePackFormat()` replaces the old `packFormatFor` guesswork. The same JSON is readable by the plain-Node build service.
6	
7	**Layout.** `lib/cyrus/engine-core/` is the game-agnostic core and must never name a game; `lib/cyrus/adapters/` holds the per-game facts.
8	
9	| File | What |
10	|---|---|
11	| `engine-core/spec.ts` | ModSpec v1 (Zod) + `validateModSpec` + `migrateSpec` + `modSpecJsonSchema()` |
12	| `engine-core/modspec.v1.schema.json` | the portable JSON Schema contract; regenerate with `npx tsx scripts/cyrus-modspec-schema.ts` (a test fails while it is stale) |
13	| `engine-core/identifiers.ts` | namespaces, identifier formats, glyph codepoints, `detectCollisions` (pure) |
14	| `engine-core/revisions.ts` | manifest validation, `diffManifests`, engine record (pure) |
15	| `engine-core/store.ts` | the only writer of the four tables (server only) |
16	| `engine-core/router.ts` | deterministic capability router |
17	| `engine-core/asset-gate.ts` | plan-tier asset gate + router downgrade |
18	| `adapters/types.ts`, `adapters/minecraft.ts`, `adapters/index.ts` | `GameAdapter` contract, adapter #1, `getAdapter(game)` |
19	
20	**ModSpec v1.** `schemaVersion` (1), `game` (adapter id), `target.version` (must be in the adapter's version registry; a preview version is valid but warns `version_not_buildable`; `blocked` is an error), `namespace` (the project's reserved `nx_<8>`), `summary`, `routes` (plugin / resourcePack / dataPack / clientMod), `requirements` with stable ids `REQ-1..` and priority must/should/could, `nonGoals`, `constraints`, `assets` slots `{ id, kind: texture|sound|model|ui, purpose, source, requirementIds }`, `tests` (acceptance plan `T-1..`: compile / scan / boot / functional / manual, `covers` REQ ids), `install` (side, restartRequired, clientSteps, notes). Unknown keys are rejected. Validation never throws: it returns `{ ok, spec | errors, warnings }`, each issue `{ path, code, message }` (codes include `missing_schema_version`, `schema_too_new`, `no_migration`, `unknown_game`, `unknown_version`, `duplicate_id`, `unknown_requirement`; warnings `untested_requirement`, `route_unsupported`, `asset_kind_undeliverable`). Migrations: `SPEC_MIGRATIONS[n]` rewrites version n to n+1; empty while v1 is the only version. Asset `source`: `generate`, `library`, `upload`, `edit` bring new or changed content (gated); `existing`, `imported` keep what the project holds (never gated).
21	
22	**Projects and revisions** (`store.ts`). `createProject({ userId, game, title?, rootBuildId? })` reserves a unique namespace (`namespaceFromSeed(projectId)`, retried with a new seed on a clash; `rootBuildId` optionally links a ModBuild chain, unique). `addRevision(projectId, { kind: generated|edited|imported|asset, manifest, spec?, modBuildId?, engine?, status?, message?, expectedHeadId? })` validates the spec (and that its game/namespace are the project's), the manifest (`[{ path, sha256, role }]`, safe relative paths, unique, stored sorted) and the engine record (prompt version, sheets with hashes, rules version, scanner hash, image digest, model, toolchain: only what is known), then appends under a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the project row: gap-free `seq`, `parentId` = previous head, head moves; `expectedHeadId` gives an optimistic `stale_head` refusal. `setRevisionStatus` is the one allowed change: pending -> passed | failed, once; a pass becomes `lastPassingRevisionId` only if it is newer than the current one, so a later failure never loses the last good revision. `getHead`, `lastPassing`, `listRevisions`, `diffRevisions` (added / removed / changed files), `revertTo(projectId, targetId)` = a NEW `revert` revision copying the target's spec, manifest, build link and status (`revertOfId`, `engine.revertOf`); history is kept. `recordAsset` stores content-addressed assets (same content twice = one row). Errors are `EngineStoreError` with a `code`.
23	
24	**Immutability in the database.** Section 2 of the manual migration adds a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger on `CyrusRevision`: any change to content columns raises, and `status` may only go pending -> passed | failed. `prisma db push` does not create triggers, so it is applied by hand with the migration (the DB test applies the same SQL to its throwaway DB). Deletes stay allowed (account/project deletion).
25	
26	**Namespaces and identifiers.** Kinds `item`, `model` (path with `/`), `sound` (dotted), `permission` and `config` (`nx_x.a.b`), `command`, `recipe`, `glyph`; `buildIdentifier(ns, kind, key)`, `parseIdentifier`, `validateIdentifier(kind, id, ownNamespace)`. `CyrusIdentifier` is unique per (namespace, kind, key); `reserveIdentifier` is idempotent. Glyphs: each namespace has a home block of 256 codepoints in the supplementary Private Use Areas (U+F0000 and U+100000 planes, 510 blocks; the crowded BMP PUA is not used); a full block moves on to the next. `codepoint` is unique across ALL projects, so Mod Packs cannot collide on glyphs. `detectCollisions(records)` (pure) reports duplicate ids (case-insensitive), duplicate codepoints and invalid ids across any set: a project, a pack, a server.
27	
28	**GameAdapter** (`adapters/types.ts`, MASTER-PLAN 4.10): artifact types per route with availability `available | planned | unsupported`, default route, toolchain profile (compiler, release per version, scanner path), knowledge source, version list with capabilities, asset delivery per kind, install rules, test lane, maturity (`planned | template | beta | stable`) and the router's `routeRules`. **Minecraft** (`adapters/minecraft.ts`) reads the version registry and `lib/cyrus/games/minecraft.ts` and changes neither; maturity `beta`; only `plugin` is available today; `resourcePack` and `dataPack` are `planned`; `clientMod` is `unsupported`; all four asset kinds deliver via a server-pushed resource pack (planned); boot/functional tests `planned`.
29	
30	**Capability router** (`router.ts`, no AI call). `routeSpec(spec, adapter, { prompt?, gate?: { plan } })` matches the adapter's rules against summary + requirements + asset purposes + prompt (never non-goals or constraints) and asset kinds, and returns `routes`, split into `available / planned / unsupported`, a `label` (`plugin`, `plugin+resourcePack`, `dataPack`, ... or `clientMod-unsupported`), `buildableNow`, `limits` (`info | warn | block` with plain-English text) and the matched rule ids. Minecraft limits: custom blocks, free-form HUD widgets, keybinds and custom sky need a client mod; native entity models need a client mod (skinned vanilla mobs / display entities instead); Dialog API needs 1.21.7+; item models need 1.21.4+; worldgen needs a restart; a preview or unknown target version blocks; planned routes say "not built yet". With `gate`, the asset gate runs first and strips gated assets (warn limits `asset_gate:<id>`), and a gated asset named only in words adds a `<rule>:plan` notice instead of a route.
31	
32	**Plan-tier asset gate** (`asset-gate.ts`, owner decisions). `canAsset(plan, kind, op)`: `create` and `edit` (also automatic generation inside a build, library picks and uploads) need `saka` for sound and `all` for texture; `model` and `ui` follow texture (top plan). `keep`, `install`, `export`, `rebuild`, `import` (your own mod) and `compose` (Mod Packs) are never gated, for any plan or none. Unknown plan / token state -> `plan_unknown` denial for create/edit only (fail closed). `normalizePlan` is the one mapping of plan names (`all` = `yakko` = "All models"; free, katara, saka). `gateSpecAssets` lists denials (the build service request must run it again), `downgradeSpecAssets` strips gated slots with a customer-visible reason and leaves requirements in place. Wiring into `gateBuild`/`create.ts` is left for the asset slice (R1): builds carry no spec or assets yet, so there is nothing to gate there today.

121	
122	**How a pack reaches players (the design).** A mod's resource pack zip is published once to object storage, named by its SHA-1, at `<public base>/p/<sha1>.zip` (immutable). Nxeon makes sure the managed **Nxeon Pack Loader** plugin is on the server (ref-counted by the mods that need it), then writes `plugins/NxeonPackLoader/packs.json` listing every Nxeon pack for that server. The plugin sends each pack on join with `Player#addResourcePack(UUID, url, sha1, prompt, force)`, so several packs stack (no merging in the common case). `server.properties` (one pack only) is the fallback.

151	- **API checked with javap against both paper-api jars** (`1.21.11-R0.1-SNAPSHOT`, `26.2.build.133-stable`): identical `abstract void addResourcePack(UUID, String, byte[], String, boolean)`, `removeResourcePack(UUID)`; `PlayerResourcePackStatusEvent#getID()` / `getStatus()` with statuses SUCCESSFULLY_LOADED, DECLINED, FAILED_DOWNLOAD, ACCEPTED, DOWNLOADED, INVALID_URL, FAILED_RELOAD, DISCARDED. 188	**The flow.** Build request -> server-side plan gate -> the build service's AI writes texture SPEC files (the existing DSL, Read/Write/Edit only) -> the service validates/renders/quality-checks them like code (bounded repairs) and returns them with the jar -> the portal re-validates, renders the deterministic pack through the version registry, hosts it, computes the Pack Loader entry and records a revision -> (flag-gated) the worker installs the Pack Loader and writes `packs.json` after the jar install.

190	### 1. Build request (`lib/modbuilder/create.ts`, `lib/cyrus/assets/{kinds,plan,request}.ts`)
191	- What is REQUESTED: `body.assets` (`["texture"]` or `{ texture: true }`, a request only, never a permission), asset words the Minecraft adapter's route rules recognise in the prompt / change request (`item_model` -> texture, `custom_sound` -> sound), and kinds the base build already has (a change keeps working on them). 192	- What is ALLOWED (`planBuildAssets`, pure): the R0 gate `canAsset(plan, kind, create|edit)` with the plan from the real lookup `tierOf(userId)` (CyrusPlan + admin override; a lookup error = unknown = fail closed), then the version (`itemModelDefinitions`, 1.21.4+; 1.21.1 is refused with "Custom textures need Minecraft 1.21.4 or newer ... Only creating/editing is gated.
193	- Anything refused is a DOWNGRADE: the plugin is built anyway and one customer-visible notice per kind is stored in `ModBuild.cyrus.assets` (`requested`, `allowed`, `notices`, `projectId`, `namespace`; read by `readCyrusMeta`) and returned as `assetNotices` by the builds API. A `ModEntry` is a plugin (descriptor + bytecode summary + jar flags), datapack index or resource-pack index, origin `server` or `candidate`, with its Cyrus namespace when built by Cyrus. Mods are sorted first; a finding id is a hash of class + subject + mods (stable, used to acknowledge a warning). Data a class needs but does not have goes to `notChecked` (never reported as clean). `normalize.ts` turns an inventory or candidate jars into entries.

313	**Merges** (`merge.ts`, inputs lowest priority first): `mergeSoundsJson` (events unioned, sounds concatenated + deduped in canonical order; a later `replace:true` drops lower sounds, reported; a lower `replace:true` plus a later plain contribution is reported as order-dependent), `mergeLang` (later wins, reported), `mergeTag` (exact Minecraft stacking: replace clears lower values, reported), `mergeAtlas` (sources concatenated), `mergeFont` (providers concatenated, codepoint overlaps reported), `mergeWholeFile` (identical collapses, else top wins, reported). Laws tested with 300 seeded cases each: idempotent (`merge([a,a]) == merge([a])`, `merge([merge(xs)]) == merge(xs)`), no key loss (tags: every value unless a reported replace), order-stable whenever no conflict is reported, deterministic bytes. `resourcepack.ts composeResourcePacks` builds one pack (or says `unmergeable` when two inputs ship shaders).

Decision: the format-aware merges above are small, pure and law-tested in TypeScript; revisit Weld behind golden tests only if datapack merging (rewriting member datapacks) becomes a requirement.

318	- **`nxpack.json`** (`manifest.ts`, Zod; portable contract `nxpack.v1.schema.json`, regenerate with `npx tsx scripts/cyrus-nxpack-schema.ts`, a test fails while stale). mrpack-shaped: `formatVersion` 1, `game` minecraft, `platform` paper, `packId` (`mp_` + 12, opaque), `versionId` (semver), `dependencies.minecraft` (registry id), `members` (id, kind plugin/datapack/resourcepack, origin cyrus/thirdparty, label, version, Cyrus `project` = projectId/revisionId/namespace, `source` provider), `files[]` = third-party BY REFERENCE (path, member, role, sha1 + sha512 (+ sha256 when known), fileSize, env server/client, https downloads), `embedded[]` = Cyrus artifacts only, at `overrides/<path>`, `overrides: ["overrides"]`, `resourcePacks` (mode `none` / `merged` (one pack) / `stacked` (ordered list), each with its Pack Loader id = UUID v5 of `<packId>:<role>`, sha1/sha256, members), `datapackOrder`, `conflicts` (counts, resolved, open + acknowledged, notChecked), `compatibility` (per version: static clean/warnings/blocked, dynamic passed/failed/incomplete/not_run, evidence), `changelog` (added/removed/updated/reordered, last 50), `build.inputsSha256`. 319	- **Builder** (`builder.ts buildModPack`, pure): inspects every member, verifies third-party bytes against the declared sha1/sha512/size when given, runs the conflict engine on members + the target server's inventory (paths the pack already owns excluded). **Only findings that involve a member count against the pack**; problems the server already had come back as `serverFindings` and never block. Refuses on any blocking finding; with `requireAcknowledged`, also on an open user-decision warning not in `acknowledge`. Resource packs: one merged pack (pack.mcmeta from the registry; 26.x refused unless `allowPreview`, same rule as `textures/pack.ts`), or `stacked` when shaders cannot merge. Version: `previous` + bump (default patch); an unchanged rebuild and a non-increasing version are refused. Compatibility rows re-run the static check per version; with no Test Flight evidence a row says `not_run (not a pass)`. Deterministic: same inputs, same archive bytes.
320	- **Install as one unit** (`install.ts`): `installModPackUnit` = validate -> fetch + verify every artifact and publish resource packs BEFORE touching the server -> preflight (never overwrite a file the pack does not own; packs.json must be valid) -> snapshot every touchable path (targets, removed targets, packs.json, the unit record, the placer's state files) with verified backup copies -> remove dropped members -> place members -> Pack Loader entries (owner `modpack:<packId>`, other owners keep their positions) -> unit record `/root/.nxeon-cyrus/modpacks/<packId>.json` -> verify. Any failure after the snapshot restores every path to its exact previous bytes (or absence), re-verifies, and reports `rollback { ok, restored, removed, mismatches }`; an incomplete rollback keeps the backup and says so. `uninstallModPackUnit` is the same transaction. Rolling back to an earlier pack version = installing that version's manifest/archive (the builder output is immutable per version). Datapacks go to `<level>/datapacks/`, config files to `plugins/<Plugin>/`.
321	- **Mods engine placer** (`engine-placer.ts`): places each member through `installOrUpdate` with a prefetched, verified resolution (package `cyrus-modpack:<packId>:<member>`, `plugin-jar` or `datapack` placement, no network) so the engine's state file knows the files; `state.json` is in the unit snapshot. **OFF** unless `CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL=1`; off, the unit refuses before touching anything.
322	- **Dynamic check** (`dynamic.ts`): `planDynamicChecks` = per version one combined boot with every member + one differential boot (all members minus M) per CHANGED member that a non-info finding links to another member; no pairwise matrix. RCON: `plugins` (all names), `help <label>` per declared command (optional, max 12), plus caller checks. `mergeDynamic`: a flight that did not complete (busy, error, missing) makes the version `incomplete` / `not_run`, never passed; per finding `confirmed` / `not_observed` / `not_observable` (classes a player-less boot cannot show: events, keys, models, single-owner, packs) / `not_run`; dynamic-only evidence: new startup error lines (combined minus differential), plugins not enabled, a command whose owner changes with M installed, missing commands. Confirmed findings are listed in the version's evidence (boot health and conflicts are different things).
323	- **Host interface for a future Mod Pack UI** (`host.ts`): `CompositionHost { openServerReadOnly, openServerForInstall (fs + base + levelName + placer), fetchArtifact, publishPack, runFlight? }` and `inspectServer(host, serverId)`, `checkAgainstServer(inventory, candidates)`, `buildAndVerify(host, BuildInput, { mcVersions, members })` (static build, flights one at a time, rebuild with evidence), `installPack(host, serverId, built)`, `uninstallPack(host, serverId, packId)`. -- CyrusRevision.modBuildId are nullable string links, no foreign keys, same convention as CyrusModPage).

Since the engine JSON is immutable, I realize the release record needs to be written at revision creation time, which works fine since sync creates the revision with the engine. But for non-asset builds where no revision exists at all, there's likely no project to attach the data to, so I need to store it only on the ModBuild metadata instead.

For asset builds, I'll pass the engine release into syncBuildAssets so it gets written at revision creation, and always write it to ModBuild.cyrus.engineRelease too. I'm now worried though — since ModBuild.cyrus is null for old UI builds, setting this field on new builds might inadvertently affect readCyrusMeta's behavior, so I should check meta.ts to see if result or publicResult would be safer places to store the engine release. For the TestFlight report, since the revision is immutable, I'm considering whether a separate additive table like CyrusFlight makes more sense than trying to force it into the existing revision structure.

Since the trigger for revision immutability likely can't be modified, and the flight runs as an async worker step after the revision already exists, I'm settling on creating a dedicated CyrusTestFlight table rather than storing it on ModBuild. For deliveries, I'm leaning toward reusing the existing Job table's payload field as a discriminated record rather than introducing a separate CyrusDelivery table.

For the gate itself, I think a worker sweep similar to sweepModBuilds makes sense—picking succeeded builds without a testflight record, capped to one flight at a time, with retry/backoff tracked via a status field with attempts and nextAt. I'd hook this into the existing sweep mechanism in worker/index.ts behind a CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE flag, since a sweep fits flights better than reusing the job mechanism meant for delivery.

I also need a per-build cost cap: limit flights per build with an attempts cap and total time budget, plus a CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL flag that blocks installs and publishing when a flight fails boot — meaning I need to find where install/publish checks happen and add a pure `flightBlocks(meta)` function to hook in minimally. The NxLabs mod page should also surface per-check statuses via the doc and view files.

Now I'm turning to the delivery orchestrator, the biggest piece, starting from existing building blocks like installModPackUnit's snapshot/rollback logic using UnitFs and MemberPlacer.

I want to reuse that snapshot machinery, so I'm reading through install.ts, the deliver.ts files for datapacks/creatures/packhost, handoff.ts, managed/service.ts, and the testflight client/runner to figure out how to run real node-2 test flights against a disposable test server directory with restart and health checks — since the runner currently only does a single boot. The real test case: deliver a mod plus a pack and datapack onto a fresh test server, confirm it boots healthy, then push a deliberately broken worldgen pack to prove rollback restores a bootable server. ### 4.4 Generators, build and reproducibility (M)
Deterministic generators emit code/data/packs for common mechanics from the IR; free-form AI code is the fallback. Build: `javac` per version lane (JDK 21 and JDK 25 side by side, per-version `--release`, classpath files fetched by checksum, exact stable pin), scan, package. Make jars byte-stable (`jar --date`, sorted inputs); record **engine release id** (prompt version + sheets + rules + scanner hash + image digest), source/classpath/output hashes, scan report and SBOM per artifact. Rename CYR-004 to "immutable javac/classpath/template".

### 4.5 Managed plugins, Pack Loader, pack hosting (M)
- **ManagedPlugin** records: pinned version per Minecraft family, installed on first dependent mod, ref-counted, not user-removable while depended on. Hosts the Pack Loader and BetterModel.
- **Nxeon Pack Loader**: sends N packs by UUID with `addResourcePack`, per-pack required/optional, accept-rate telemetry, Geyser/Floodgate detection. `server.properties` only as fallback. Conflict engine detects an existing pack owner (ResourcePackManager, Oraxen, Nexo).
- **Pack hosting**: object storage on an Nxeon domain (provider not named to customers), content-addressed immutable URLs `/p/<sha1>.zip`, size caps, retention GC; keep it off the primary node.

### 4.6 Test Flight (M, lite first)
Disposable Paper server per target version on node-2 (MEASURED 2026-10-10 with Test Flight lite: 26.x 10.4-10.8 s boot, 722-803 MB peak RSS; 1.21.11 on JDK 21 18.0 s, 878 MB; whole flight 12-20 s; see docs "Cyrus Test Flight (R0)"): boot, plugin enabled, RCON commands, `datapack list`, log matcher, clean shutdown. Later: MockBukkit logic tests, Mineflayer scenario bots (MIT, supports through 26.1), performance scenarios. Honest per-check status table; no "success" if a required stage was skipped. Concurrency capped (a past node crash came from parallel builds).

### 4.7 Asset pipeline and studios
Shared studio core + per-game profile. Minecraft = pixel profile.
- **Texture** (top plan): LLM writes a pixel spec (palette + shapes), deterministic renderer draws it (raise the 400-op / 16-64 px limits for skins and larger atlases), optional pixel-model candidates later; per-mod **Style DNA** (palette ramps, outline rule, noise) for consistency; per-version validation; AI edits arrive as non-destructive candidates.
- **Sound** (Saka+): `SoundSpec` (events -> layers -> processing); tag the 514-file library by filename category; synthesis presets; processing in the browser from WAV, **server-side ffmpeg/libvorbis to mono Ogg Vorbis**; new namespaced sound keys played by the plugin (and silence the vanilla base mob; never override vanilla keys globally); mandatory subtitle keys. A complete mob set: ambient, hurt, death, step, attack, ability, spawn.
- **Models** (26.x first): `RigSpec` compiled by Nxeon code (3 archetypes, 5 procedural clips) to .bbmodel for **BetterModel** (MIT, pinned managed plugin). Handgun and similar items use static item models with display transforms, sounds and particles, no engine. Do not embed Blockbench (GPL app); do not depend on ModelEngine/FreeMinecraftModels/CraftEngine.
- **Quality bar**: rubric + metrics (texture palette size, contrast, edge density, banding, transparent policy; sound mono, true peak, loudness band per role, silence ratio) plus a vision-model judge calibrated on 100 owner-labelled samples; owner reviews a gallery.
- **Studios**: v1 minimal (miniPaint MIT stopgap or a small pixel editor; wavesurfer.js BSD waveform with trim/fade/layer and JSON edit recipes), then the full editors in R3. Library browsing follows the studio gate.

### 4.8 Conflict engine and Mod Packs (L)
- **Server inventory** first: read-only scan of jars' descriptors, `server.properties`, datapacks, existing pack owners. This is the conflict engine's input (and the "Server Doctor" feature below).
- **Static classes**: plugin names, commands/aliases (incl. Brigadier root literals and vanilla overrides), permissions, depend/softdepend/loadbefore DAG, api-version/Java/Folia, registered events + priorities, NamespacedKey/PDC keys, legacy `custom_model_data` integers and `item_model` keys, recipe keys, sound event keys, single-owner resources (Vault economy/permission provider, chat renderer, tab list, sidebar, world rules), datapack `replace:true` tags and double-overridden vanilla ids, resource-pack whole-file overrides, `sounds.json`/atlas/lang merges, font codepoint overlap, unmergeable shaders, budget classes (display entities, tasks, pack size).
- **Resolution**: reserved namespaces prevent most clashes; command alias rewrites; priority ordering; Pack Loader stacking; evaluate Weld/Beet (MIT) as an offline merge subprocess behind golden tests. Severity report: blocking / warn / info.
- **Dynamic**: one combined boot and one differential boot per changed mod; pairwise only for statically flagged pairs.
- **Mod Pack**: an Nxeon manifest shaped like mrpack (files with path/sha1/sha512/downloads/env, override dirs, platform=paper). Third-party jars by URL + hash, only Cyrus-built artifacts embedded. Versioned, changelog, compatibility matrix, combined test report; installs and rolls back as one unit; never contains Paper/vanilla jars. Not gated by plan.

**Engine layers**
1. **Mod project model (the "source").** A typed, versioned project: ModSpec / content IR (items, mobs, abilities, GUIs, quests, recipes, loot, biomes...), code files, assets (textures, models, sounds), data packs, configs, dependencies, tests. Stored as revisions (like git): every change is a diff, every revision reproducible and revertible. The chat history is not the project.
2. **Registries.** Capability registry (what each game/version can do), version registry, **identifier registry** (namespaced IDs for items, models, sounds, commands, permissions, recipes, glyphs), asset registry with licence/provenance. Registries are authoritative for routing, validation, conflict detection and UI.
3. **Generators (compilers).** Deterministic generators turn the IR into code, data packs and resource packs for common mechanics; free-form code generation is the fallback for the unusual. The AI is the **author/planner/editor** that proposes IR changes and writes custom logic; the engine validates and builds. Users can also edit the project directly through designers and studios, with no prompt needed.
4. **Validators + build.** Schema validation, compile, scan, asset validation, pack validation, per-version checks. No stage is skipped silently.
5. **Test Flight (runtime harness).** Real disposable server, mock tests, bot scenarios, performance checks, honest per-check statuses.
6. **Composition layer.** **Conflict engine** + **Mod Packs** (combine mods and assets, resolve or flag clashes, test the combined result, install and roll back as one unit).
7. **Importer.** Bring a mod you own into the engine as revision 0 and keep working on it (see Top priorities below).
8. **Editors.** Texture Studio, Sound Studio, data/GUI/quest/boss designers, ability graph: all edit the same project model.
9. **Delivery + lifecycle.** Pack hosting and multi-pack merge, install/uninstall/update/rollback, diagnostics, version upgrade assistant, NxLabs publishing with evidence-backed labels.
10. **Per-game adapters** on a shared core (Foundation Principle below).

## TOP PRIORITIES (owner, 2026-10-09)
1. **Asset Libraries + Studios, gated by plan tier** (see "Plan-tier gating"). A **Sound Library** (the owner's original 514-file library, tagged, plus synthesized presets, plus the customer's uploads) with the **Sound Studio**; a **Texture Library** (vanilla-style presets, customer uploads) with the **Texture Studio**. Libraries feed Cyrus's automatic asset generation. Every asset carries provenance and licence.
2. **Mod conflict engine + Mod Packs.** Real logic when combining mods or adding several Cyrus mods to one server: detect conflicts before install, resolve what can be resolved, and **compile mods into a versioned Mod Pack** tested as a whole.
3. **Bring your own mod.** Upload a mod you own (source project, jar, datapack/resource pack), work on it in Cyrus, and **build it with Cyrus** (edit by prompt or designers, rebuild, scan, test, version, install).

content.thinking:
The engine also keeps its own backup folder that prunes old entries to 5 — since pruning could delete an older backup mid-operation, I can't reliably restore that without snapshotting the whole folder first, so I'll just document it as out of scope for the restoration.

On the config side, the engine only copies the plugin's own folder as backup and doesn't delete it on uninstall, so that's fine to leave as-is.

So I'm pinning down the orchestrator's exact snapshot scope: top-level plugin jars, the pack loader's packs.json, the mod state file, datapack top-level files, BetterModel's config and model files, the mod pack unit records, any plugin config files touched per the pack plan, and our own delivery record used for uninstall/update — plus the relevant directories listed non-recursively.

For verification I need a hash of each backed-up file, but reading every jar over SFTP to compute sha256 is expensive. I'm weighing whether to cap total snapshot size and refuse oversized deliveries, or push the hashing to the remote side via an exec call added to SshGuestFs — though that touches Nxeon code. Simpler path: define an optional sha256 method on the filesystem interface that defaults to reading the file locally, letting the host adapter override it with a faster remote implementation if available.

Actually, maybe I don't need full hashing at all — rollback could just copy back every backed-up file unconditionally using remote cp, which is byte-exact and cheap, verifying only touched files with full hash while verifying untouched ones just by size against the snapshot's stat listing.

That raises a concern though: restoring files while the server is still running risks corrupting an open jar if cp rewrites in place, so the server should be stopped before restore and only started again afterward.

A simpler path occurs to me: since the orchestrator controls every write, I can wrap the filesystem handed to inner installers in a recording proxy that tracks each writeFile, rename, remove, or copy target, snapshotting originals before their first mutation.

This gives copy-on-write backups — only touched files get read and hashed, and rollback becomes a reverse replay of the journal, restoring or deleting as needed. The remaining question is how this proxy plugs into the Nxeon host's managed installer, which receives its own fs through an open() call.

I think the design should have the orchestrator open the server to get the raw GuestFs, wrap it in a JournalFs, and pass that journaled fs into every host operation (jar placement, unit install, creature delivery) so all mutations funnel through the same journal, including the engine's own backup-directory writes which would then also get rolled back correctly.

For pruned backups, since removal of a directory means the journal would back up that entire tree recursively (potentially huge for jar backups), I need to exclude paths under `/root/.nxeon-mods/backups` from journaling entirely as a pass-through, and document that -- our own journal backup dir should be pass-through too. For renames, the journal needs to record both the source and destination paths so a crash can be reversed properly, and for partial file writes going to a `.nxeon-part` path, the journal should record the absence of that path so rollback deletes it. I'm also planning persistence: writing the journal to disk after each entry under a transaction-specific path on the server, so a crashed delivery can be recovered via a `recoverJournal` function.

Rather than auto-recovering, I decide the safer approach is to detect a leftover journal on the next delivery attempt and refuse until an admin runs a recovery step -- I'll add a preflight check for pending journals and a `recoverDelivery()` function that performs the rollback. For the DB side, managed plugin references snapshot and restore through the host's managed snapshot API, and since published packs are immutable and content-addressed, rollback doesn't need to undo pack publishing since garbage collection handles unreferenced content. I'm also sketching the restart/health flow -- calling host restart and health check functions that return status reports with plugin states, error lines, and loaded datapacks, with the real server variant using game-power restart and SSH log reads, and the test variant using a Test Flight run. Now I'm working out the rollback sequence for when a failure happens after restart but the health check fails.

For jar replacement under a running JVM, I realize overwriting in place is risky but renaming a new inode into place is safe since the old inode stays open -- so the restore logic should copy the backup to a temp part file and atomically rename it into place rather than copying directly over the original. I'm also noting that jar changes typically require a restart since the server doesn't hot-load plugins, and currently the existing tooling just reports that a restart is needed without actually performing it.

For the restart decision itself, I want the orchestrator to only restart or reload exactly as the apply semantics require, but auto-restarting a customer's server is a real behavior change, so I'm considering a restart policy of "now" versus "next_restart" — defaulting to immediate restart since deferring is dangerous for worldgen or creature changes where no one would catch a failed startup later. I'll make next_restart only permitted when the change contains no worldgen or creature hand-off, otherwise refusing it at preflight with a clear reason, while datapack-only changes can just be reloaded without any restart at all.

For health checks, after a restart I want the server to respond via console/RCON, confirm the expected plugins are enabled, and show no new error lines compared to a baseline captured during preflight — normalized by stripping timestamps so I'm only catching genuinely new errors. For datapacks I'll check that the enabled list contains the loaded file, and for worldgen I'll look for the server's "Done" boot line as confirmation.

Then after restart I need to trigger the BetterModel hand-off, which reads the build archive, publishes it, and upserts the loader entry, followed by a Pack Loader reload via console or file watch. I'm now thinking through how `deliverMod` should resolve a project revision into a concrete release — assembling a "ModRelease" object from the revision and build that captures the namespace, Minecraft version, plugin details (name, jar, checksum), and optional resource pack and datapack metadata.

The host's `loadRelease` builds this release from the ModBuild result, jar file, and rebuilt datapacks, giving the orchestrator a pure data object to work with. From there, jar placement goes through the Mods engine via a GameMod/ServerMod row, with the orchestrator calling installer methods that different hosts implement differently — Nxeon uses its catalog-based installer, while fake hosts use a simpler filesystem placer. For mod packs, `deliverModPack` follows the same orchestrator pattern but installs as a journaled unit, with restart semantics triggered when the unit requires it.

I'm now thinking through the generic transaction engine itself: `runDelivery` takes a plan and host, executing pluggable mutation steps within a journal, each recorded as a StepResult with status and timing. The steps start with journal recovery checks, then preflight inventory scanning and conflict detection (which can block or just warn), followed by baseline health capture, then ensuring managed plugins like Pack Loader or BetterModel are present before finally publishing the pack itself.

The remaining steps cover updating Pack Loader config, placing jars/datapacks/models and config files, applying a restart or reload as needed, running a health check, handling BetterModel's post-restart hand-off plus loader reload, and finally committing the delivery record while cleaning up journal backups. Any failure from step three onward triggers a full rollback — restoring the journal and refs, restarting if needed, and verifying the rollback brought the server back up successfully.

I also need to work out the master feature flag that gates delivery entirely, plus per-component flags for managed plugins, datapacks, modpacks, creatures, and worldgen. When a release includes a component whose flag is off, I'm deciding whether to skip just that piece with a note or block the whole delivery — leaning toward skipping to stay consistent with how pack delivery already behaves when disabled, and treating worldgen-off as implying datapack-skip too, matching existing deliverDataPack logic.

I'm designing the delivery record stored per project that tracks the jar target, datapack files, creature models, loader ids, managed keys, and worldgen dimensions, so updates and uninstalls can reference what was actually installed. For uninstall I'm planning to remove the jar, listed datapacks, pack loader entry, and creature models, release managed plugins via ref-counting with a journal, but deliberately leave world folders for dimensions intact — surfacing them in the result as keptWorldFolders for manual admin cleanup, since those require a restart to take effect.

For snapshot/restore of managed plugin refs, I'm adding `snapshotServerManaged` and `restoreServerManaged` to the managed service: restore walks each key, updating the row to match the snapshot if it existed, or deleting it if it didn't, all inside a transaction with row locking to keep it safe under concurrent access.

For real Nxeon servers, I still need a host-level implementation of restart and health checks over SSH -- likely using the existing game-control controlSpec for restart (similar to how GAME_POWER triggers a restart) and reading logs via GuestFs or RCON for health. I should check lib/game-control and worker/mod-health to see how restart and log-based health checks are currently wired up before building the Nxeon adapter.

content.thinking:
I'm starting to write the cyrus-delivery worker module, importing the database, sandbox, guest filesystem abstractions, and SSH-based guest connection tools it'll need.

Still importing dependencies...

I'm sketching out the delivery payload shape for the Cyrus job system, then drafting the job handler that reads the payload, checks the feature flag, and fetches the server record with its related templates and plan data.

Next I resolve the delivery host, branch on uninstall versus deploy (loading build artifacts and calling the release/deliver functions), then persist the result back onto the job record and write an audit log entry. I'm weighing whether a failed-but-rolled-back delivery should throw and trigger a retry, since that seems wrong for cases where the failure was already handled gracefully.

On rollback failures, I'll avoid throwing and instead call `noRetry(job.id)` to cap the retry attempts before throwing an error, so the job ends up FAILED without being retried. I'm also noting that ServerMod row syncing isn't needed here, since this orchestrator path is specifically for Cyrus delivery jobs rather than the general mod-sync flow.

Though actually, since the engine's installed package tracking doesn't create a GameMod row on its own, I need to update the ServerMod row (status, versionId, fileName) after a successful install when `serverModId` is provided, so installed mods still show up correctly in the Mods tab.

For `realSession`, I'm implementing the restart flow: send the restart command over SSH, parse the response code and state, then poll the server's log file every few seconds for a "Done (" line that appears only after the restart, comparing against the pre-restart log content since Paper rotates the log file fresh on each start.

For health checks, I need to parse the log for successful startup, plugin enable/disable events, error lines before the "Done" marker, and confirm the server is responsive via rcon list and datapack commands. The real server base path is `/opt/mc`, and I'll read the level name from server.properties via the filesystem, using null for the Minecraft version so the orchestrator falls back to inventory data.

Now I'm setting up the managed port with a journaled filesystem dependency object.

Still writing dependency setup...

Writing plugin resolution logic...

The JournalFs needs a cast since its `kind` field is optional but GuestFs requires it to be strictly "ssh" or "local".

Still writing the jar installer logic...

Checking the catalogFacts signature uses targetVersionId, and ensureCyrusGameMod lives in the Nxeon-side registry lib which is fine to call from the worker. For the sandbox session, I'm using LocalGuestFs rooted at the sandbox, with restart returning ok:true and real health checks.

## Cyrus integration and delivery (R5)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r12` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 4.4 (engine release id), 4.5, 4.6, 4.8, R0/R2 and "Engine layers" 9 (delivery + lifecycle). **Nothing is deployed or switched on; no migration, no new table, no new enum value.** Everything new is behind OFF flags: `CYRUS_DELIVERY` (master switch of the orchestrator), `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE`, `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL`, and the sound relay env; each delivery part stays behind its existing flag (`CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL` (+ `CYRUS_WORLDGEN`), `CYRUS_CREATURES`, `CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL`). With all of them unset the only behaviour change is that a succeeded build gets an `engineRelease` key in its `ModBuild.cyrus` JSON (bookkeeping, stripped from customer views).

**Host seam.** `lib/cyrus/delivery/*` and the gate never import Nxeon internals beyond what Cyrus already used (`mods/guest-fs` types, `db` in the existing `*-worker.ts` pattern, lazily). Nxeon implements the small interfaces in the worker: `worker/cyrus-delivery.ts` (server file access through `SshGuestFs`/`LocalGuestFs`, the Mods-engine Cyrus installer, restart through the existing `powerScript`, RCON through `runRcon`, managed-plugin refs through `lib/cyrus/managed/service.ts`, pack hosting through `selectPackStore`). No new logins, plans or tables: Cyrus stays inside Nxeon and can stand alone later by re-implementing `DeliveryHost`.

### 1. Engine release record (`lib/cyrus/engine-core/release.ts`, `services/modbuilder/release.js`)
"Prove what built every mod." The build service attaches `release` to every succeeded build record (and a service summary on `/health`): base prompt version + per-section prompt versions (assets, datapack(+worldgen), design, itemmodel), knowledge version, API sheet name + sha256, rules version + sha256, scanner (`scan.js`) sha256 + scan profile (strict / attested), registry file sha256, JDK release + `javac -version`, classpath file sha256, the allowlisted compile-only dependencies used (id + sha256 = SBOM-lite), toolchain line, image version. Anything it cannot read is `null`, never guessed.
`buildEngineRelease()` (pure) merges that with what the portal knows (the jar sha256 it re-hashed after download, its own registry hash, `/health` cached 5 min as a fallback for older images) into `{ schema: 1, id: "er1-<20 hex>", recordedAt, target, prompts, knowledge, sheets, rules, scanner, service, registry { portal, service, match }, jdk, artifact { kind: jar, name, sha256 }, classpathSha256, sbom, toolchain, model, unknown[] }`. `id` is the ENGINE identity (hash of the engine facts, not of the artifact / deps / model): two builds with the same id came from the same engine release. `verifyEngineRelease` recomputes it (detects an edited record); `readEngineRelease` reads it back.
Stored (`lib/modbuilder/store.ts`): on `ModBuild.cyrus.engineRelease` for EVERY succeeded build (atomic `jsonb ||` merge via `mergeCyrusKey`, so a concurrent project patch cannot drop it), and, when the build gets a revision (asset builds), on `CyrusRevision.engine.release` at creation (revisions are append-only; the trigger forbids later engine edits). `readCyrusMeta` passes `engineRelease`/`testFlight` through (bounded), `toView` strips `engineRelease` from customer views. Existing rows are untouched (no backfill). A failure to build or store the record only logs; it never fails a build.

### 2. Test Flight gate (`lib/cyrus/testflight/gate.ts` pure, `gate-worker.ts` worker; sweep `cyrus-testflight-gate` every 2 min in `worker/index.ts`)
OFF unless `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE=1` (checked before any import or DB read). Each tick takes recent (7 days) succeeded builds without a stored result (or whose busy retry is due) and runs ONE flight through the existing injectable invoker (`runTestFlight`, ssh to node-2) with the build's jar, its data packs (rebuilt deterministically from the stored specs) and, when the Pack Loader jar is available on the worker (`CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGIN_DIR`), the pack config it would get. RCON: `plugins` (must list the plugin), `help <label>` per declared command (max 8, optional), `nxpacks status` with a pack. Only versions with a pinned Paper SERVER build fly; others are stored as "not run: no test server for <version>". Limits: one flight per worker at a time (node-2 serialises too), `busy` re-queued with exponential backoff (30 s .. 10 min, max 12), at most 2 real flights per build (per-build cost cap; a transport error counts), a build whose scan BLOCKED is not flown.
Result on `ModBuild.cyrus.testFlight` (`StoredFlight`): state (queued / running / done / not_run / gave_up), six honest checks `compile, scan, boot, plugins_enabled, commands_registered, datapack_loaded` each pass / fail / not_run (a runner "pass" with no evidence is `not_run`; "not run" is never shown as passed), verdict (passed / failed / incomplete / not_run), runner + Paper build + JDK, boot time, peak RSS. The label is only ever `boot-tested on Paper <version>` (a boot proves the plugin loads and its commands register, never in-game behaviour); a failed `commands_registered` is shown but does not fail the verdict (labels come from the build's summary and can differ from the registered names). The NxLabs page (`lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts` `testFlight`, `CyrusModView` "Boot test") shows the head line + the six statuses; the page is regenerated when a result becomes final.
Optional block (`CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL=1`, `flightBlocks`): a version whose flight FAILED is not installed (`loadCyrusJar`, `installBuildToServer`) or published (`setCyrusPageVisibility` PUBLIC). "Not run" never blocks.

### 3. Delivery orchestrator (`lib/cyrus/delivery/{types,plan,journal,orchestrator,release,admin}.ts`)
`deliverMod(serverId, release, host)` / `updateMod` (same call; an existing on-server record makes it an update) / `uninstallMod(serverId, projectId, host)` / `deliverModPack` / `uninstallModPack`. ONE transaction-like sequence, each step timed and recorded (`steps[]`):
1. `open`, `recover_check` (a left-over journal from a crashed worker REFUSES the delivery until an admin runs `recoverJournal`), `preflight`: release bytes verified (jar sha256, pack sha1, data pack sha256; worldgen must be `restart`), parts whose switch is off left out with a note, creature models re-compiled and checked, the server inventory scanned and the conflict engine run on the candidates against what the server runs (our own previous files excluded): blocking findings REFUSE (nothing changed), warnings recorded; the Pack Loader config must be valid. Mod Packs re-check their member jars against the LIVE server the same way.
2. managed-plugin refs snapshot (database rows), then `managed` (ensure Pack Loader for a pack, BetterModel for creatures; release what the previous version needed and this one does not), `host_pack` (immutable URL), `pack_config` (upsert / remove this mod's entry, owner `project:<id>`; other owners' entries keep their positions; an existing pack owner is noted), `place` (jar through the host's installer, data packs as `<level>/datapacks/nxeon-<ns>-<name>.zip`, BetterModel config + models; files of the previous version that are gone are removed), `record` (`/root/.nxeon-cyrus/deliveries/<projectId>.json`).
3. `apply` only as the semantics require (`planApply`, pure): plugin jar / managed plugin / registry content (enchantments) / world generation / creature models -> restart; reloadable data pack only -> `minecraft:reload`; Pack Loader config only -> `nxpacks reload` (its file watch also picks it up). `restartPolicy: "next_restart"` defers a restart (outcome `pending_restart`, not health-checked) and is REFUSED for world generation and creatures (a broken pack stops the server at its next start, so those need a supervised restart).
4. `health` (`judgeHealth`): the server came up (for worldgen: actually reached Done), answers commands, every expected plugin enabled (removed ones gone), no NEW error lines (compared with the pre-change log), every data pack loaded; a simulated probe is never a pass. `handoff` (creatures, after the restart): BetterModel's `build.zip` published and pointed at by the Pack Loader. `commit` drops the journal.
5. ANY failure after preflight -> ROLLBACK: the copy-on-write journal restores every file the delivery or any installer it called touched (bytes verified against the recorded sha256; new files and folders removed), the managed refs are put back to the snapshot, and when a restart or reload had happened the server is restarted (reloaded) again and must come up; outcome `rolled_back`, or `rollback_incomplete` (journal + backups kept, next delivery refused) when anything could not be verified or the server did not come back.
**Journal** (`journal.ts`): every mutation goes through `JournalFs`; before the first mutation of a path it copies the file to `/root/.nxeon-cyrus/delivery-journal/<id>/b/<n>` (server-side `cp`, then re-read and compared) or records it absent / its folder tree / the parent folders a write creates; the journal JSON is persisted after every entry. Restores are written as a new file + rename (never in place under a running JVM). Not journaled (documented): the Mods engine's own rotating backup folder and the Mod Pack unit's backup folder; file ownership (`chownLike`) is not restored.
**Uninstall**: jar, data packs, models and the pack entry are removed, managed plugins released (ref-counted: the Pack Loader stays while another mod needs it). A dimension's world folder (`<level>/dimensions/<ns>/<dim>`) is KEPT (players' builds live there) and listed in `keptWorldFolders` for an admin cleanup action; nothing deletes world data automatically.
**Mod Packs** go through the same transaction: the R2 unit installer (`installModPackUnit`) writes through the journal with the host's member placer, so the pack is still one unit and a failed restart/health check after a successful unit install is rolled back too. `lib/cyrus/modpack/host.ts` `deliverPack` / `undeliverPack` are the entry points a UI uses. A Mod Pack's data packs are treated as restart content (the unit cannot tell reloadable from registry content).
**Release assembly** (`release.ts releaseFromBuild`, pure): jar (sha256 re-checked), the hosted pack (status `ready` only), data packs rebuilt from their stored specs to the recorded sha256, creatures from the stored rows.
**Worker wiring** (`worker/cyrus-delivery.ts`): a `GAME_MOD_SYNC` job whose payload carries `{ cyrusDelivery: { v: 1, op: "deliver" | "uninstall", buildId | projectId, serverModId?, restartPolicy? } }` (payload discriminator on an existing job type; ordinary payloads never carry it) is handed to `cyrusDeliveryJob`, which refuses unless `CYRUS_DELIVERY=1`, builds the release, runs the orchestrator with the Nxeon host and stores the compact result on `payload.result.cyrusDelivery` (+ audit log; a failed delivery is not retried). Nothing enqueues such a job yet. In SANDBOX the health probe is `real: false`, so a delivery that needs a restart is rolled back honestly (use `next_restart` there).

### 4. Sound render path (`lib/cyrus/sound/relay.ts`, `host.ts selectRenderHost`)
The web process never connects to node-2: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` is refused inside Next.js (`NEXT_RUNTIME` set). Owner configuration:
- worker: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh`, `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_PORT=<port>` (e.g. 7351), `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_TOKEN=<random, >= 24 chars>` (+ the existing optional `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER_HOST/_ROOT`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_DIR`, `CYRUS_SOUND_FFMPEG_DIR`): the worker starts a loopback-only relay (`127.0.0.1`, bearer token, 4 MB request cap, one job at a time) in front of `sshRenderHost`.
- web: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=relay`, `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, the same token. Build syncs and the Sound Studio's "Render and preview" / library audition go web -> worker -> node-2. The library-gated preview still needs `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`.
- health probe: `GET /health` on the relay (and `probeSshRenderHost`): ssh reachable, ffmpeg runs, library file count, work dir writable. No audio is rendered or stored on the primary (the relay forwards JSON only).

### 5. Admin visibility (`lib/cyrus/delivery/admin.ts`, `GET /api/admin/cyrus/ops?limit=`)
Read-only JSON, same gate as `/admin/cyrus` (role + "modbuilder" preview list), no UI: `deliveries` (GAME_MOD_SYNC jobs with the discriminator: op, outcome, failed step, error, steps, rollback incl. restart + health after rollback, notes), `flights` (per build: state, verdict, label, six checks, reason), `engines` (engine id, prompt, scanner, image, unknown), and `passRates` per Minecraft version from stored flights (`flown / passed / failed / incomplete / notRun / passRate`; only completed flights count, "not run" is counted apart and never as a pass) for a future public pass-rate page.

### 6. Tests and real runs
- RAN on devhost: `test/cyrus-delivery.test.ts` (33: plan + health judge, flag off = server never opened, fresh install, a fault injected at EACH step (managed, host_pack, pack_config, place, record, apply, health) restores the exact bytes + folders + refs, an EXHAUSTIVE run that fails every single file operation of a delivery in turn and checks the exact restore each time, restart fails once (rolled back + restarted) / always (`rollback_incomplete`, files still exact), a broken worldgen pack that stops the server (rolled back, restarted, came up), a plugin that fails to enable, update v1 -> v2 with a fault at each step restoring v1 exactly, reload-only change, blocking conflict refusal, switches off, restart policy, bad bytes, uninstall with faults + dimension folder kept, shared Pack Loader ref-count, journal crash recovery, Mod Packs install/uninstall/faults/live conflict/flag), `test/cyrus-gate-release.test.ts` (12: engine record determinism / identity / tamper / fallbacks / meta round trip / service half on real files; gate planning, honest statuses, failed boot + block flag, incomplete, busy backoff + caps, no server pin, sweep off/one-per-tick), `test/cyrus-relay.test.ts` (4), DB (`devhost db push`, then `CYRUS_DELIVERY_DB_TEST=1 npx tsx --test test/cyrus-delivery-db.test.ts`, 5: refs snapshot/restore, a real-service delivery whose health fails restores the rows exactly, concurrent jsonb merges keep every key, admin JSON-path query + pass rates, engine release on a revision).
- RAN REAL on node-2 (raw: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/delivery-r5-flights-2026-10-10.json`): `devhost run -- npx tsx test/cyrus-delivery-real.ts --local`. The orchestrator drove a disposable server dir under `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-r12/`; every restart booted the dir's CURRENT contents on real Paper 1.21.11 b132 / JDK 21.0.12 with Test Flight, and the health probe read that flight. A: fresh delivery (TfItemModel fixture jar + Pack Loader + packs.json entry + the data pack studio showcase) -> `delivered`, healthy (boot 18.9 s, 896 MB). B: update adding a deliberately BROKEN worldgen pack -> the server did not come up (boot_done fail, registry errors) -> rolled back (1 file restored, 1 removed, refs restored) -> restarted on the previous state -> came up healthy (18.1 s) -> `rolled_back`, the dir's tree hash equal to before the update (exact restore). C: update with the VALID worldgen showcase -> `updated`, came up with the dimension pack loaded (19.9 s, 924 MB). D: uninstall -> `uninstalled`, jar + packs gone, Pack Loader released, healthy boot. Five flights, one at a time, no busy; the run dir was removed afterwards.
- RAN REAL gate flights (`test/cyrus-gate-real.ts`, raw `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/testflight-gate-r5-2026-10-10.json`): TfHello on 1.21.11 -> passed, "boot-tested on Paper 1.21.11", commands registered (boot 18.5 s, 868 MB); TfBroken on 26.2 -> failed (plugins enabled FAILED), blocks only with the flag; a 26.3 build -> not run (no test server), no flight.
- RAN REAL relay (`test/cyrus-relay-real.ts`, raw `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/sound-relay-r5-2026-10-10.json`): relay -> real render host on node-2: health ok (ffmpeg n8.1.3, 514 library files, work dir writable), the synth-only example set rendered (3 events, 5 mono Vorbis files) in 0.7 s.
- **NOT RUN**: no real customer server, no production DB, no real bucket; the Nxeon host adapter (`worker/cyrus-delivery.ts`: ssh restart + log parsing + RCON health) was type-checked but never pointed at a real Nxeon game server; creature hand-off ran only with fakes (BetterModel needs 26.2 + seeded libraries); no player joined any flight (packs, gameplay unverified); the gate was not run from the worker sweep against real ModBuild rows; the relay was not run inside the real worker / Next.js processes.

### Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- Test Flight results live on `ModBuild.cyrus.testFlight`, not on the revision: revisions are append-only (DB trigger forbids engine edits after creation) and many builds have no revision; a revision reaches its flight through `modBuildId`. No table was added.
- Deliveries are recorded on the GAME_MOD_SYNC job row (payload discriminator + `payload.result.cyrusDelivery`), not a new table; the on-server record + journal hold what a rollback needs.
- Health fails on NEW error lines (vs. the pre-change log) by default (`strictLog`); after a rollback only "came up" is judged (the previous state's own log is not ours to judge).
- A delivery restarts the server when the change needs it (`restartPolicy` "now" by default); worldgen and creatures can never be deferred.
- Data packs in mod deliveries are placed through the journaled fs (not the Mods engine placer); the on-server delivery record knows them. Mod Pack data packs are treated as restart content.
- Delivery of a part whose flag is off is a note, not a failure (same as R1); the master flag off refuses everything before the server is opened.
- `commands_registered` failures are shown but do not fail the gate verdict; a scan-blocked build is never flown; max 2 flights per build.

### Owner actions (nothing needed to merge; nothing to approve as a migration)
1. No migration / enum / table. The R0-R4 owner steps still come first (engine-core + managed-plugin migrations, catalog seed, pack storage + domain, Pack Loader jar on the worker host).
2. Rebuild the build-service image (Dockerfile now copies `release.js`) so builds carry the service half of the engine record; until then the record falls back to `/health` and lists the gaps in `unknown`.
3. Gate: set `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE=1` on the worker (one flight per 2 min max, ~20 s and ~1 GB on node-2 each); decide `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL` (default off); pin Paper server builds for more versions to fly them.
4. Delivery: wire an enqueue path (route/UI) that creates the GAME_MOD_SYNC job with the `cyrusDelivery` payload, do ONE supervised real delivery on an owner test server, then `CYRUS_DELIVERY=1` on the worker. Decide whether automatic restarts are acceptable for customers (default: restart when needed) and the admin cleanup action for kept dimension folders.
5. Sound: set the relay env on the worker and `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=relay` + URL + token on the web process (never `ssh` there).
EOF
echo done

**Journal** (`journal.ts`): every mutation goes through `JournalFs`; before the first mutation of a path it copies the file to `/root/.nxeon-cyrus/delivery-journal/<id>/b/<n>` (server-side `cp`, then re-read and compared) or records it absent / its folder tree / the parent folders a write creates; the journal JSON is persisted after every entry. Restores are written as a new file + rename (never in place under a running JVM). Not journaled (documented): the Mods engine's own rotating backup folder and the Mod Pack unit's backup folder; file ownership (`chownLike`) is not restored.
**Uninstall**: jar, data packs, models and the pack entry are removed, managed plugins released (ref-counted: the Pack Loader stays while another mod needs it). A dimension's world folder (`<level>/dimensions/<ns>/<dim>`) is KEPT (players' builds live there) and listed in `keptWorldFolders` for an admin cleanup action; nothing deletes world data automatically.
**Mod Packs** go through the same transaction: the R2 unit installer (`installModPackUnit`) writes through the journal with the host's member placer, so the pack is still one unit and a failed restart/health check after a successful unit install is rolled back too. `lib/cyrus/modpack/host.ts` `deliverPack` / `undeliverPack` are the entry points a UI uses. A Mod Pack's data packs are treated as restart content (the unit cannot tell reloadable from registry content).
**Release assembly** (`release.ts releaseFromBuild`, pure): jar (sha256 re-checked), the hosted pack (status `ready` only), data packs rebuilt from their stored specs to the recorded sha256, creatures from the stored rows.
**Worker wiring** (`worker/cyrus-delivery.ts`): a `GAME_MOD_SYNC` job whose payload carries `{ cyrusDelivery: { v: 1, op: "deliver" | "uninstall", buildId | projectId, serverModId?, restartPolicy? } }` (payload discriminator on an existing job type; ordinary payloads never carry it) is handed to `cyrusDeliveryJob`, which refuses unless `CYRUS_DELIVERY=1`, builds the release, runs the orchestrator with the Nxeon host and stores the compact result on `payload.result.cyrusDelivery` (+ audit log; a failed delivery is not retried). Nothing enqueues such a job yet. In SANDBOX the health probe is `real: false`, so a delivery that needs a restart is rolled back honestly (use `next_restart` there).

### 4. Sound render path (`lib/cyrus/sound/relay.ts`, `host.ts selectRenderHost`)
The web process never connects to node-2: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` is refused inside Next.js (`NEXT_RUNTIME` set). Owner configuration:
- worker: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh`, `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_PORT=<port>` (e.g. 7351), `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_TOKEN=<random, >= 24 chars>` (+ the existing optional `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER_HOST/_ROOT`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_DIR`, `CYRUS_SOUND_FFMPEG_DIR`): the worker starts a loopback-only relay (`127.0.0.1`, bearer token, 4 MB request cap, one job at a time) in front of `sshRenderHost`.
- web: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=relay`, `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, the same token. Build syncs and the Sound Studio's "Render and preview" / library audition go web -> worker -> node-2. The library-gated preview still needs `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`.
- health probe: `GET /health` on the relay (and `probeSshRenderHost`): ssh reachable, ffmpeg runs, library file count, work dir writable. No audio is rendered or stored on the primary (the relay forwards JSON only).

### 5. Admin visibility (`lib/cyrus/delivery/admin.ts`, `GET /api/admin/cyrus/ops?limit=`)
Read-only JSON, same gate as `/admin/cyrus` (role + "modbuilder" preview list), no UI: `deliveries` (GAME_MOD_SYNC jobs with the discriminator: op, outcome, failed step, error, steps, rollback incl. restart + health after rollback, notes), `flights` (per build: state, verdict, label, six checks, reason), `engines` (engine id, prompt, scanner, image, unknown), and `passRates` per Minecraft version from stored flights (`flown / passed / failed / incomplete / notRun / passRate`; only completed flights count, "not run" is counted apart and never as a pass) for a future public pass-rate page.

### Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- Test Flight results live on `ModBuild.cyrus.testFlight`, not on the revision: revisions are append-only (DB trigger forbids engine edits after creation) and many builds have no revision; a revision reaches its flight through `modBuildId`. No table was added.
- Deliveries are recorded on the GAME_MOD_SYNC job row (payload discriminator + `payload.result.cyrusDelivery`), not a new table; the on-server record + journal hold what a rollback needs.
- Health fails on NEW error lines (vs. the pre-change log) by default (`strictLog`); after a rollback only "came up" is judged (the previous state's own log is not ours to judge).
- A delivery restarts the server when the change needs it (`restartPolicy` "now" by default); worldgen and creatures can never be deferred.
- Data packs in mod deliveries are placed through the journaled fs (not the Mods engine placer); the on-server delivery record knows them. Mod Pack data packs are treated as restart content.
- Delivery of a part whose flag is off is a note, not a failure (same as R1); the master flag off refuses everything before the server is opened.
- `commands_registered` failures are shown but do not fail the gate verdict; a scan-blocked build is never flown; max 2 flights per build.

input.message:
All five pieces are built and committed on `feature/cyrus-r12` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r12`). Nothing is deployed or switched on. The real node-2 runs passed, including a broken worldgen pack that stopped the server and was rolled back to the exact previous files.

**What I built**
- **Engine release record:** `services/modbuilder/release.js` plus `lib/cyrus/engine-core/release.ts`. It is stored on `ModBuild.cyrus.engineRelease` for every succeeded build, and on the revision's `engine.release` when the build gets a revision. Customer views strip it.
- **Test Flight gate:** `lib/cyrus/testflight/gate.ts` and `gate-worker.ts`, run by a worker sweep. Each build gets six statuses (compile, scan, boot, plugins enabled, commands registered, data pack loaded). The only label is "boot-tested on Paper X", shown on the NxLabs page. Optional flag to block install/publish of a failed build.
- **Delivery orchestrator:** `lib/cyrus/delivery/{journal,plan,orchestrator,release,admin,types}.ts`. The worker side is `worker/cyrus-delivery.ts`, reached through a payload marker on the existing `GAME_MOD_SYNC` job type. Nothing enqueues such a job yet. Mod Packs go through the same orchestrator (`modpack/host.ts deliverPack`).
- **Sound render path:** `lib/cyrus/sound/relay.ts`. The web process goes through a loopback relay in the worker, never directly to node-2, and the relay has a health check.
- **Admin read model:** `GET /api/admin/cyrus/ops` (read-only JSON: deliveries, flights, engine records, pass counts per version).

**How rollback is proven:** every file write goes through a journal that backs up each path and checks its hash before the first change. The tests inject a failure at every step, and in a separate run at every single file operation in turn; each time the server folder hashes identical and the plugin refs match. Restart failures and "server didn't come up after worldgen" are covered too. On node-2, the bad-worldgen update rolled back and the server came up on the old state.

**Ran / not run**
- Ran: 4 delivery scenarios on real Paper 1.21.11, 3 gate flights and a real sound render through the relay. Results are in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/{delivery-r5-flights,testflight-gate-r5,sound-relay-r5}-2026-10-10.json`. Also 5 DB tests on the throwaway DB.
- Not run: the worker side against any real Nxeon server, creature hand-off with real BetterModel, any player join.

**Flags (all off):** new `CYRUS_DELIVERY`, `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE`, `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL`, and the relay env. Every existing per-part flag still applies.

**Owner approval:** no migration, table or enum. The build-service image needs a rebuild (it now copies `release.js`).

**Merge:** latest `feature/cyrus-r2` (menu + quest designers) merged with no conflicts; artifact checks current, tsc clean, 1580/1580 tests pass. The first run after the merge failed two pipeline tests because my `javac -version` call confused the fake javac; the JDK version is now read from the JDK's `release` file instead.

**Decisions the plan didn't specify**
- Flight results live on the build record, not the revision (revisions can't be edited after creation).
- Deliveries are recorded on the job row.
- Health fails on new error lines.
- Worldgen and creatures can't defer their restart.
- Kept dimension world folders are listed for an admin to clean up.
- At most 2 flights per build.
- A failed command check is shown but doesn't fail the verdict.
- Mod Pack data packs get a restart.

Docs are in the "Cyrus integration and delivery (R5)" section of `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`; `OWNER-ACTIONS.md` is updated.
